question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Battles of European Rivalry]
options: Battle of Wandiwash (1760) — Decisive British victory ending French ambitions in the Carnatic
Battle of Bedara (1759) — English defeat of Dutch forces, ending Dutch political aspirations in India
Battle of Plassey (1757) — British victory over Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah of Bengal
Battle of Buxar (1764) — Decisive French victory over the combined forces of the Mughal Empire and Bengal Nawab
wrong_fact: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought and won by the British East India Company (led by Hector Munro) against the joint forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah, and Shah Alam II. The French had no role in this battle.
explanation: The Battle of Wandiwash (1760) established British supremacy over the French. The Battle of Bedara (1759) crushed Dutch power in Bengal. Plassey (1757) began British political dominance in Bengal. Buxar (1764) confirmed British control over Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha, and reduced the Mughal emperor to a British pensioner.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Treaty Territorial Adjustments]
options: Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748) — Restored Madras to the British in exchange for Louisbourg in North America
Treaty of Paris (1763) — French factories restored in India but they were forbidden to fortify them
Treaty of Ryswick (1697) — Restored Pondicherry to the French after Dutch occupation
Treaty of Allahabad (1765) — Ceded administrative control of Goa to the English East India Company
wrong_fact: The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) granted the Diwani rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha to the British East India Company. It did not involve Goa, which remained under Portuguese administration until 1961.
explanation: The Treaty of Allahabad was signed between Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II and Robert Clive following the Battle of Buxar. The treaties of Aix-la-Chapelle (1748), Ryswick (1697), and Paris (1763) were international settlements that reshaped the territorial holdings of European powers in India.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Puppet Rulers and Regional Alliances]
options: Muzaffar Jung — French-supported claimant installed as Nizam of Hyderabad in the Deccan
Chanda Sahib — French ally who claimed the Nawabship of the Carnatic against Anwar-ud-din
Muhammad Ali — British-backed claimant who successfully held the fort of Trichinopoly
Mir Jafar — Dutch ally installed as Nawab of Oudh to block British expansion in northern India
wrong_fact: Mir Jafar was installed as the Nawab of Bengal (not Oudh) by the British East India Company (not the Dutch) following the Battle of Plassey (1757) as a puppet ruler.
explanation: During the Carnatic Wars, Dupleix supported Chanda Sahib in the Carnatic and Muzaffar Jung in Hyderabad, while the British backed Anwar-ud-din (and later Muhammad Ali) in the Carnatic and Nasir Jung in Hyderabad. Mir Jafar was the commander-in-chief of Bengal who betrayed Siraj-ud-Daulah to help the British win Plassey, and was subsequently made Nawab of Bengal by Clive.
